chunks: And ʿUmar ibn Ḥanẓalah narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who sold a piece of land on the basis that it contained ten jarībs, and the buyer purchased that from him with its boundaries, paid the price, concluded the sale transaction, and they parted; then when the land was measured, it turned out to be five jarībs.

He عليه السلام said: If he wishes, he may recover the excess of his money and take the land; and if he wishes, he may rescind the sale and take all of his money back, unless the seller also has lands adjoining the boundary of that land, in which case he completes it for him, and the sale becomes binding upon him, and fulfillment for him is by the completion of the sold property. But if he has nothing else in that place besides what he sold, then if the buyer wishes, he may take the land and recover the excess of his money; and if he wishes, he may rescind and take all of the money.

key_terms.أَرَضُونَ: other lands owned by the seller nearby
key_terms.أَرْضًا: a parcel of land being sold
key_terms.الثَّمَنَ: the purchase price paid by the buyer
key_terms.بِتَمَامِ الْمَبِيعِ: by completing the full amount of the sold property
key_terms.رَدَّ الْبَيْعَ: to rescind or cancel the sale
key_terms.عَشَرَةَ أَجْرِبَةٍ: ten jarībs, the claimed land measurement
key_terms.فَضْلَ مَالِهِ: the excess portion of the buyer's money that should be returned

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if purchased land turns out to be smaller than the amount stated in the sale?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling for a land sale where the actual measured area is less than what was represented at the time of sale. The buyer is granted the option either to keep the land and reclaim the overpaid amount or to rescind the transaction entirely, unless the seller can complete the deficient amount from adjoining land.
